title: Turn Meeting Notes into Actions, Then Reconcile Them
subtitle: Use AI to structure the mess; verify owners, decisions, and dates before publishing
description: After a meeting, use AI to convert permitted notes or a transcript into decisions, actions, owners, dates, and open questions. Then reconcile the structured output against the original record before it becomes the team's memory.

lifeOsSource.hack: Convert meeting notes into a structured action register with AI, then verify each decision, owner, and due date against the meeting record.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Use only notes or transcripts you are allowed to process. Ask for five buckets: decisions, actions, owners, dates, and unresolved questions. Compare each populated field with the source, remove inferred commitments, and publish the checked version quickly while context is fresh.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Does every named owner and commitment come from the meeting, or did the model quietly turn a suggestion into an assignment?

faq.question: What is the main failure mode?
faq.answer: The model can infer an owner, deadline, or decision that sounded plausible but was never agreed. Those fields deserve explicit reconciliation.

faq.question: Can I upload any meeting transcript?
faq.answer: No. Follow your organization's privacy, confidentiality, retention, and approved-tool rules. Sensitive content should not be sent to an unapproved service.

intro.html: Meeting notes often fail in the boring gap between conversation and ownership. AI can help close that gap, but it is very capable of making an unassigned action look pleasantly assigned.

sections.title: 1. Use an approved record
sections.html: Start with notes or a transcript you are permitted to process. Remove unnecessary sensitive information before sharing it with any external tool.

sections.title: 2. Ask for a fixed schema
sections.html: Request decisions, action, owner, due date, evidence from the notes, and open questions. A fixed schema makes omissions and unsupported fields easier to spot.

sections.title: 3. Reconcile commitments
sections.html: Check names, dates, decisions, and obligations against the original record. If ownership was not explicit, write “unassigned” rather than accepting an AI guess.

sections.title: 4. Publish the checked record
sections.html: Send or store the reconciled version while the meeting is still fresh enough for people to correct it. The human-approved record becomes the source of truth, not the transcript summary.

editorialCuration.reason: A low-risk transformation workflow with explicit privacy and reconciliation gates; no unsupported claim that AI meeting notes improve team performance.
